newsitem.title: UK: Start-up of UK gas competition "too fast" - Giordano.
newsitem.headline: Start-up of UK gas competition "too fast" - Giordano.

text.p: Competition in the UK's domestic natural gas industry should have been phased in over several years, not the two or three years allowed by industry regulator Ofgas, chairman of the former British Gas plc told reporters on Thursday.

"The pace of change was obviously too fast and that largely was caused by the timetable for the introduction of competition by 1998," said Richard Giordano. He added that it would have been better to phase in competition over five years.
And charges relating to the introduction of competition cost the company around 220 million stg, Giordano added.

He said that 1996, British Gas's last year as a single entity, had been characterised by system problems with Centrica, the new company which will take over domestic supply; by extra expenditure related to the introduction of the Network Code, the "rule book" for trading gas in the deregulated market; and by extra expenses for services.

"The aggregate for these one-off charges was about 220 million stg," he said. This eradicated some of the higher revenue the company received as a result of colder weather in 1996 than in 1995, and also higher revenues from the industrial and commercial sectors.

"And then you get the exceptionals," he added. British Gas saw exceptional charges totalling 1,138 million stg on a historical basis, of which the largest item was contract losses and renegotiations, totalling 635 million stg.
"These had to be done, it's the only way forward," he added.
Earlier this month, British Gas demerged its gas supply business into a new company, Centrica Plc, and changed the name of its remaining gas transport and storage business to BG Plc.
